Real-repo reviewer startup with the spec base: ready true, testChanges present with 70 testFiles, all undeclared, 453 featurePaths. About 55 of the 70 are not tests (receipt logs, review reports, spec markdown, skill text, test-changes.mjs itself) matched by the [AC: substring rule; see f11-3.

findings.summary: Deleted and renamed tests lose identity. git diff --name-only uses rename detection, so a renamed test lists only its new path (tests/old.test.ts -> tests/renamed.test.ts gives only tests/renamed.test.ts); a declaration under the old path never matches and the deletion is invisible. A deleted file that is a test only by its [AC: tag (checks/verify.ts) is dropped, because read() returns "" for a missing file. Brief class 3 is exactly deleted tests. Fix: pass --no-renames, and for deleted paths read the base bytes (git show <base>:<path>) when testing for [AC:. Receipt spec-11-probe.log section 2.
findings.assumption: The spec's checks cover added/modified files only; the coordinator may treat this as blocking since spec 17 will judge deletions from this list.

findings.summary: isTestPath implements exactly the spec's list, which misses common layouts: segments are case-sensitive (Swift Tests/), Android src/androidTest and Kotlin src/jvmTest, C# App.Tests/FooTests.cs, Java FooTest.java outside src/test, Ruby app/x_spec.rb outside spec/, Python tests.py and conftest.py, JS e2e/*.e2e.ts and *.cy.ts. False positives: docs/spec/overview.md and src/test_helpers_shared.ts. Files with an [AC: tag or a check input are still caught. Suggest case-insensitive segments, segments ending in Test/Tests, and names matching (Test|Tests|_spec)\. before the extension.
findings.assumption: The spec names the convention list; matching it literally passes spec-11-1.

findings.summary: Any changed file whose text contains "[AC:" counts as a test. On this repository with spec 11's own base, startup lists 70 undeclared "test files", about 55 of them not tests: review receipt .log files, review-*.report.json, spec markdown, payload/.agents/skills/joycraft-verify/SKILL.md, and test-changes.mjs itself; featurePaths then has 453 lines, mostly from spec and report text. Spec 17 will judge undeclared entries, so this noise recreates the false-flag problem the feature fixes. Suggest applying the tag rule only to files outside the features folder and with a code extension, using trace.mjs's tag regex, or only to check inputs. Receipt spec-11-startup-base.log.
findings.assumption: The spec literally says "holds an [AC: tag", which these files do; the defect is in the definition, so it does not fail spec-11-1.

findings.summary: A changed submodule (a directory path in git diff) makes read() throw EISDIR, so the whole result is lost; in startup it becomes testChanges.error. Guard read() with a file check. Receipt spec-11-probe.log section 3.
findings.assumption: Submodule bumps are rare in Joycraft projects.

findings.summary: A Test changes bullet with a backticked path relativePath refuses (e.g. `../outside.test.ts`) throws and loses the whole result instead of skipping that bullet. Receipt spec-11-probe.log section 5.

A wrong --changes-base gives ready: true with testChanges: {error}. Startup is not stopped, so a reviewer who reads only undeclared sees nothing. The spec does not decide this; the error is visible in the output. A ref name (HEAD, origin/main) is refused by the sha regex, consistent with "startup never guesses a base".
findings.assumption: Reporting the error and continuing is the reading closest to "startup is unchanged" without the list.

findings.summary: Commit 82fce24 also edits an existing test outside the spec's file list while ## Test changes says none: afterEach rmSync gains maxRetries: 5. No assertion, skip or expected value changed; it does not weaken the test. Noted for the declared-test-changes rule only.
findings.assumption: A cleanup-retry tweak is not a weakened test.
